You Know Animal-Print Rugs, But Do You Know Animal Pictorials? (2026)

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1395 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the oldest known pile rug—pulled from a frozen tomb in Siberia in 1949—features a procession of 24 fallow deer and a parade of men on horseback.
  • Rajaram is describing a literal animal rug, also known as an animal pictorial.
  • According to recent reports, “What we’re seeing now is a shift toward rugs where the whole animal is part of the design and has a role in the composition,” indicates Kerri Anne Besse, design director at rug brand Tumble.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the oldest known pile rug—pulled from a frozen tomb in Siberia in 1949—features a procession of 24 fallow deer and a parade of men on horseback. Some 2,500 years after its creation, animal illustrations are making their way back onto the floor. A serpent coils through the Snake and Pomegranate rug by Christopher Farr and Studio Shamshiri in Lucy Hale’s Los Angeles home, and a Tibetan tiger stretches across Demi Lovato’s modern farmhouse and Ethan Cook’s SoHo loft. These aren’t spots or stripes standing in for a neutral—they’re meant to be noticed and discussed. “Animal print is a texture; an animal motif is a story,” indicates AD100 designer Pavitra Rajaram, who recently designed Bahaar, an animal-themed rug in her Majnun collection for Jaipur Living. “I think people are tired of decoration that says nothing and are looking for objects that carry meaning.”.

Rajaram is describing a literal animal rug, also known as an animal pictorial. These playful floor coverings often feature a bucolic scene of several animals or a single animal form woven into the textile, and they come in styles ranging from avant-garde and surrealist to Art Deco and folk-inspired.

A master bedroom by Studio Duggan.

According to recent reports, “What we’re seeing now is a shift toward rugs where the whole animal is part of the design and has a role in the composition,” indicates Kerri Anne Besse, design director at rug brand Tumble. “The oversized, blown-up animal print feels dated.”.

It has been revealed that as for styling, Sophie Salata, head of brand at Vinterior, recommends that designers let the pictorials stand on their own. “I’d be inclined to treat the rug almost as a piece of art, allowing it to become a focal point rather than trying to make everything around it match,” she says. Pamela Marshall, creative director at artisanal rug brand Patterson Flynn, agrees with this approach: These designs are more than backdrops.

Reformation's nine-piece rug collection with Les Éditions de Tapis includes depictions of cats, swans, and tigers.

Recently, brands have been launching their own interpretations of animal pictorials. Last week, Reformation debuted its first-ever home collection, a collaboration with Les Éditions de Tapis that features hand-drawn swans and cats. At Milan Design Week this year, Fornasetti launched a surrealist-inspired line of rugs with CC-Tapis depicting slithering serpents from the luxury designer’s archive. A few months earlier, Ruggable released its collaboration with Scalamandré to bring the upscale design house’s iconic zebras to more homes. And in October 2025, Nordic Knots launched its Swedish Grace collection, including the Grace 03 Fauna rug, which reveals a wildlife scene. Looking further back, Beni’s serpent rugs have been a designer favorite since 2020.

Industry observers note that one of the earlier examples of literal animal rugs is a collection between longstanding collaborators Patterson Flynn and AD100 designers Charlap Hyman & Herrero. It grew from a one-off rug into a full collection of graphic natural-and-black silhouettes that launched in 2018 and continues to expand. “Areas of inspiration for these come from Calder’s simplified animal forms, the surrealists’ play on scale, and 17th-century cabinets of curiosity, to name a few,” claims Marshall, who credits Hyman’s “encyclopedic” design references for the originality. We would be remiss not to mention Diane von Furstenberg’s long-running collaboration with the Rug Organization, which has been producing the iconic Climbing Leopard rug since 2005.

Rugs from Charlap Hyman & Herrero x Patterson Flynn’s collaboration.

The Rug Company x Diane von Furstenberg Climbing Leopard rug in emerald.

In a recent development, these rugs’ rich history might be part of their renewed appeal. Animals have been a subject for as long as people have made pictures. The oldest known figurative cave painting—found in Indonesia and dated to at least 51,200 years ago—highlights a wild pig with three human figures.

“Animals have shaped our textiles and rugs for longer than we think,” indicates Bella Valenzia, founder of Pelican House, pointing out that animal forms have appeared in tapestries and wall coverings, and as functional home objects, such as pelt and hide rugs used for warmth and comfort, since the earliest days of humankind. “We like to think it is part of a wider return to folk-inspired, storytelling textiles, with a sense of nostalgia,” she adds. Pelican House’s rug Frith references the old English countryside, where horses have long been at the heart of rural life.

Various animals, real and mythical, carry their own significance across cultures, and their meaning can deeply influence a home’s design. For example, a pictorial of a lion, which signifies power in certain cultures, adds a very different element to a space than a fish, which can signify good luck, notes Jahanshah “Josh” Nazmiyal of Rug & Kilim. Veronica Renton, senior vintage and antiques specialist at 1stDibs, adds that peacocks often signal nobility and immortality.

Plenty of designers still reach for the originals: While the contemporary versions of these rugs are having a moment, their earlier counterparts remain relevant. “I particularly love antique Tibetan tiger rugs and Persian and Chinese rugs featuring guardian lions, dragons, and all manner of mythical beasts,” notes Tiffany Duggan, founder of Studio Duggan.

The Tiger Rug by Studio Ashby in Sophie Ashby’s former home in London.

Where these rugs live in the home is likewise important. Naturally, the pieces work well in spaces that are meant to be playful, like nurseries and children’s rooms. For example, in this garden apartment designed by Rebecca Benichou and Florence Jallet of Batiik Studio, the Toulemonde Bochart Lion rug brings a spot of levity to a windowless craft room. In the bedroom of Kate Upton and Justin Verlander’s daughter, Genevieve, designed by John Ruggiero, the Doing Goods Blooming Black Bear Rug provides a spot of whimsy. For double the fun, designer Olivia Song put two animal rugs, the Doing Goods Pinky Lion and Pinky Leopard, in her nephew’s room in this Sag Harbor beach home.

That said, these rugs work in more adult spaces, too. “In the [primary] bedroom of one of our London projects, we used the beautiful Snake and Pomegranate rug,” indicates Duggan. “I love the way the snake weaves its way around the bed, creating a focal point and bringing a little humor and unexpected character to an otherwise calm space.”.

Sources indicate that designer Rayman Boozer from Apartment 48 has a rug with a large tiger on it from the Rug Organization in his own home. “Animal motifs can sometimes feel juvenile, but there’s something refreshing about bringing that sense of playfulness into a sophisticated space,” he claims.

Rayman Boozer’s home, featuring an Apartment 48 tiger rug.

Steven Loloi, co-principal at Loloi, agrees. Speaking of Loloi’s Roam collection that released last month and features cheetahs, zebras, elephants, and giraffes in neutral colors, he highlights the surprising versatility of the pieces, which he notes can fit just as nicely in a bedroom or living room as in a lounge or den. “I think we’re seeing people become more confident in their design choices and a little less concerned with playing it safe,” he says. “Why not have a leopard or zebra in your living room?”.

It’s worth noting that these rugs aren’t for everyone, and some designers avoid any type of animal rug because of the hunting culture they reference. Others, though, embrace them as a way to reimagine humanity’s relationship to animals and commit to living better by them.

It has been revealed that rajaram's Bahaar rug does just that with its contemporary expression of 'shikargahs,' the enclosed forests where kings hunted at leisure, which are celebrated in Iranian and Mughal design. “Instead of being chased, the animals are in harmony with each other, frolicking freely in the forest. It’s a celebration of coexistence rather than conquest,” she says. The Charlap Hyman & Herrero x Patterson Flynn collection had a similar ambition: “Our Tigre and Oso nod to traditional hide floor coverings; they give you the drama of the trophy rug without the trophy,” notes Marshall.

It has been revealed that on the surface, the return of these animal-forward rugs might have looked like a change in aesthetics, but it’s really much more anthropological. “We have always gravitated toward pieces with animals, and even in modern production, history is repeating itself,” notes Nazmiyal. Some 2,500 years after their first spotting, these animal-clad rugs are back home.

Breaking: You Can See Everything You Ever Want to See in a Movie in You Can See Everything

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • NATHAN FIELDER HAS become one of the greatest arbiters of what is—or isn’t—the truth.
  • Industry observers note that the road for Fielder has included HBO’s The Rehearsal (another often surreal, often Lynchian project that presents as real, but on a subtextual level asks viewers to question whether any of what he’s depicting was really happening as it was shown) and The Curse, a Showtime/Paramount+ series that he starred in and co-created alongside Emma Stone and Benny Safdie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

NATHAN FIELDER HAS become one of the greatest arbiters of what is—or isn’t—the truth. Fielder, whose mainstream career unofficially kicked off with his show Nathan for You, a dry, quasi-documentary, quasi-scripted, quasi-spoof of indicates like Undercover Boss, has found a way to level up with each project he’s made over the course of his still relatively short career, each step of the way inviting audiences to not only question the reality of what he’s bringing to the screen, but their own stances and ways of thinking about things broadly.

Industry observers note that the road for Fielder has included HBO’s The Rehearsal (another often surreal, often Lynchian project that presents as real, but on a subtextual level asks viewers to question whether any of what he’s depicting was really happening as it was shown) and The Curse, a Showtime/Paramount+ series that he starred in and co-created alongside Emma Stone and Benny Safdie. That show was, surprise, surprise, incredibly thoughtful, layered, and, ultimately, surreal when it comes to its underlying themes of sincerity and intention.

It has been revealed that in a way, all of this has led Fielder to his latest project, the new A24 documentary You Can See Everything. The subject is a fitting one for Fielder: Elizabeth Holmes, the former Theranos CEO and convicted fraudster who was the subject of books (Bad Blood) and television demonstrates (The Dropout) about her misdeeds. It makes total sense that someone famous for skirting the truth would be of interest for Fielder, a creator who has now spent so much time examining not only the truth, but what audiences might accept as the truth even given some reason not to.

Sources indicate that in 2022, Holmes was sentenced to 11 years and 3 months in federal prison. That’s where You Can See Everything comes in: Holmes and her partner Billy Evans invited Fielder (and a film crew, led by co-director Lance Oppenheim) to join them in a home they were renting for complete access during the 34 days before she reported to federal prison in Bryan, Texas, in May 2023. And the film begins there.

And, quite frankly, if you’re considering seeing You Can See Everything, it’s best to leave it there. Fielder gets the access he was promised in the movie, but the joy of the film isn’t only in this exclusive vision of such a notable figure, but how an artist with such a relationship to the truth engages with someone who so notably has, seemingly, bent it. We also get to see Holmes and Evans shot as human beings, removed from any of the prior media circuses that have surrounded them. Fielder and Oppenheim put a fair camera to everything and let the camera do what was promised: See everything.

You Can See Everything has been one of the best-reviewed films of the year, and it lives up to the billing. Just when you think you understand what’s happening and what’s going to happen, you’ll be swiftly proven wrong. Just when you think you have a handle on who someone is and what they’re all about… you’ll quickly be proven wrong. The movie is three hours long, which, of course, we know, seems daunting. But by the time it ends, you’ll wish it was going on for three hours more.

Below, we answer some of your questions about You Can See Everything—without spoiling any of the movie’s major twists or turns.

Industry observers note that you Can See Everything is now available to watch at home. You can purchase it on Apple TV and rent it on Prime Video—and we suggest doing whichever of those you prefer.

It has been revealed that you Can See Everything is, in essence, two movies in one. The first half of the movie is what the trailer and promotional materials for the movie billed: Nathan Fielder joins Elizabeth Holmes (and her new husband Billy Evans) in a home they rented for the 34 days before she reported to federal prison in 2023. This proves to be just as compelling as you’d imagine, as Holmes and Evans are both completely idiosyncratic characters. Moments like when Fielder reveals Holmes Abbott and Costello’s “Who’s on First” bit are instant classics.

Eventually Holmes reports to prison in Bryan, Texas, and the movie is not even halfway over. It’s at this point that your eyebrow should raise, and you do the ‘leaning forward in seat’ meme—because this is when You Can See Everything gets truly wild. The timeline jumps forward two hours, and Nathan Fielder gets up to some of his mind-bending, Rehearsal-type business. At this point, we see some people’s true colors, and also meet some other unexpected guests and surprises in the movie. This second part of the movie is what will blow your mind, and leave you thinking long after the credits begin to roll.

According to recent reports, you Can See Everything should be an absolute lock for a number of Oscar nominations, including Best Picture. And it should be a strong contender in one of the acting categories for one person whose appearance we will not be spoiling in this story.

Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim are the co-directors of You Can See Everything, and both have been key figures in American film and television culture for the last decade.

Recent findings suggest that fielder is a Canadian-born actor and director (and childhood friend of Seth Rogen) who rose to fame as the creator and star of Comedy Central’s Nathan for You. He’s dabbled in acting here and there—including a role as a limo driver in Rogen’s underrated holiday comedy The Night Before and in the sensational limited series The Curse—but his real calling has come in mind-bending documentary/comedy series like The Rehearsal. In season 2 of The Rehearsal, for example, Fielder actually got his pilot’s license while exploring the aviation industry. (And that was filmed between part 1 and part 2 of You Can See Everything, which is just bananas.).

In a recent development, oppenheim, who is only 30, has also established himself as one of the best documentarians in the business. His movies Some Kind of Heaven and Spermworld along with his HBO series Ren Faire are deeply layered portrayals of very real people in very real situations; he shoots these documentaries in styles completely different from anyone else, though, lighting them like cinematic spectacles rather than what you probably think of as a documentary in your mind. (Some of the cinematography in You Can See Everything is unbelievably beautiful.).

Primetime, A24’s film about Chris Hansen and To Catch a Predator that came out last month and starred Robert Pattinson, Skyler Gisondo, and Merritt Wever, was Oppenheim’s scripted feature debut.

Sources indicate that it probably helps to have information on Elizabeth Holmes’s case—which we recommend getting from any number of sources: The Dropout was the name of the Hulu series that starred Amanda Seyfried as Holmes, but it was also a well-researched and reported podcast that served as the show’s basis. There’s also an HBO documentary called The Inventor and a book called Bad Blood. Any of this would make for a good source for the crimes Holmes was accused of committing. The movie also includes a very brief recap of her case in the early going—not exhaustive, but enough to get the idea.

Industry observers note that it does also make sense to have an idea of who Fielder is, what he does, and how he engages with his subjects. We recommend HBO’s The Rehearsal for that, but it’s not 100 percent necessary to enjoy and appreciate the film.

That’s the question, isn’t it? You Can See Everything explores the idea of truth, lies, perspective, and even documentary filmmaking itself. If it makes the most sense to you to take all of You Can See Everything at face value, then please go for it. If you feel the need to question everything, well, that’s okay too. That’s what makes Fielder’s work so unique and so immersive—you can think about it about 100 different ways, and no understanding or interpretation is wrong. It’s set up to feel like a kaleidoscope. You can understand something one way, but maybe something pops up, and suddenly you can’t think about it that way anymore. That’s the point—and that’s what you’ll think about long after the credits roll.

Waymo halts highway operation nationwide after CA DMV pause

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.
  • Waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017.
  • It has been revealed that the vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.

Waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017. It has now expanded to 15 areas, recently adding another 250 square miles just last month.

It has been revealed that the vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas. Since it can operate at any time but only within geofenced areas, this counts as “level 4” autonomy, as compared to the level 2 autonomy available on most consumer vehicles.

Sources indicate that until recently, Waymo only operated on city streets. These are more complex than highways, but lower speed. Accidents are more common on city streets than on highways, but can be more spectacular on highways given the higher speeds involved.

Recent findings suggest that most driver assist systems have been rolled out gradually, starting with highways, due to this lower complexity. But Waymo started with city streets first, bucking that trend.

Sources indicate that the company started offering rides on highways late last year, but only in limited markets. It had been testing highway operation for several years prior, typically with a driver and with no public ridership.

Everything was going pretty well, with Waymo declaring its autonomous vehicles have stopped 841 injuries over the course of their 271 million miles of operation. And in terms of competition, Waymo is far ahead of Tesla’s Robotaxi effort.

Industry observers note that but then, the viral internet stepped in. Last week, a video surfaced showing a Waymo trying to pass two police cars who were trying to slow down traffic on I-280 in Northern California. This is one of the main routes through Silicon Valley, and the opening of highway operations drastically reduced ride times in the area.

In a recent development, the video reveals two police cars behind a construction vehicle, lights on and spread out across the freeway. Then it pans to show a Waymo vehicle moving swiftly in the far left lane. One of the officers accelerates and swerves in front of the Waymo vehicle, at which point the Waymo swerves and slows down. (One media citation claims that the video seems to have been sped up by the original poster, but we’ve embedded the short local news report on it above).

In a recent development, in response to this, the California DMV contacted Waymo and ordered the organization to pause highway operations while it examines the incident. The order was made on November 11, but wasn’t reported until today.

Recent findings suggest that the DMV cited multiple instances of Waymo vehicles incurring into construction zones, not simply the one viral clip above. It said that previous incidents had occurred and been noted, and corrective actions were implemented, but that the incidents keep happening.

This is a very rare situation which Waymo handled poorly. Waymo will add this case to their their test suite. They'll probably ask the CHP for their in car videos of other cases and convert those to be additional test cases. Waymo has been very willing to admit when their vehicles make mistakes in rare situations and fix it so that it doesn't happen again.

Waymo's vehicles are compared against perfect driving and Waymo accepts that as an aspirational goal. I note Tesla lacks the confidence in their system to even apply for the California permit to begin autonomous testing.

DMV’s pause will remain until Waymo can demonstrate “effective corrective actions” have been taken.

In a recent development, while the DMV’s order only applies to California highways, Waymo also paused highway operations in other states. It remains operating on city streets in all coverage areas.

Update: Waymo emailed us this statement after it saw this article.

Sources indicate that “Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

The Best Matching Sweat Sets, Tested by Style and Fitness Editors

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2422 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in.
  • Back in the day, a sweatsuit was all about comfort.
  • Sources indicate that whether you’re the kind of person who considers it a cozy wardrobe essential, or you’re just looking to treat yourself to something comfortable to wear around the house, there have never been more choices when it comes to the best matching sweatsuits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Back in the day, a sweatsuit was all about comfort. It wasn’t so much a fashion staple, but the kind of thing to throw on and lounge in. With Y2K style back in vogue, matching sweatsuits are more commonplace than ever—just with a little less sparkle than the ones previously sported by icons like Paris Hilton and J.Lo in the early 2000s. And, with the rise of athleisure, these simple sweats have gotten the luxury treatment: they’re softer, more flattering, and pricier than ever.

Sources indicate that whether you’re the kind of person who considers it a cozy wardrobe essential, or you’re just looking to treat yourself to something comfortable to wear around the house, there have never been more choices when it comes to the best matching sweatsuits. Since we’re heading into winter (and Black Friday is just around the corner!), Women’s Health editors tested the most popular styles.

Here are our thoughts on the matching sets after months of lounging in them, working from home in them, and even wearing them to work.

Oner Active Foundations Zip Up Hoodie.

Oner Active Foundations Sweatpants.

Sources indicate that oner Active’s workout clothes have had our hearts at WH for a while. That’s why we were excited to put their loungewear to the test. Associate Health and Fitness editor Addison Aloian wore this set while traveling, chilling at home, and even working behind the scenes on a photoshoot.

“I absolutely love this set from Oner,” she says. She loves it for its comfort, warmth, and versatility (Aloian says she knows she could wear it outside in the chilly NYC winter, layer it under her ski clothes, or pop it on over leggings for her warm-up at the gym). “But the standout feature is the color,” Aloian says. “So many sweat sets are gray or black, but the turquoise is stunning and makes it a standout in my closet when I want a monochromatic moment.” She opted for the “oil blue” color, but Oner also has options like alpine green and toasted red, plus your neutral staples.

It’s also one of the more affordable options we tested—and on sale for half off this Black Friday. But that doesn’t mean it skimps on quality: The material feels super plush since it’s made from 67% cotton and 33% polyester, for a super plush feel that doesn’t pill or shed after one wash.

The set’s one flaw? The bottoms are a little long. At 5 '1, Aloian says she’d love a “short” option as well. Oner does offer a “long” length, though, for the taller girlies.

Old Navy Bounce Fleece Half-Zip Pullover Sweatshirt.

Old Navy High-Waisted Bounce Fleece Jogger Sweatpants.

In a world of expensive sweat sets, Old Navy’s Bounce Fleece line provides a budget-friendly—and stylish—option. “You’d never know these are super affordable,” states Fitness editor Cori Ritchey. They hold their own with the rest of the pricier sets from their fit to their feel.

According to recent reports, the highlight for Ritchey is the material, a mix of polyester, rayon, and spandex. “It moves with you, and the fabric feels like it breathes compared to other sweatsuits that feel too heavy and hot.” One small caveat: Be sure to follow the wash instructions and keep your cycle on cold and gentle, tumble dry low, and keep the garments inside out. Ritchey indicates she noticed a bit of pilling after the first wash, but says that after following the wash instructions during the next few washes, the set stayed in great shape.

In a recent development, the half-zip and jogger combo makes for a put-together look and is cozy enough for traveling, running errands, or lounging around the house, Ritchey claims. The set comes in plenty of neutral colors, plus some fun ones like orchid. It’s also the first on our list that doesn’t have a prominent logo, for anyone who wants a clean-looking set with no branding. Another point for Old Navy: It’s the most size-inclusive on the list. Sizing goes from XS to 4XL, with regular, tall, and petite options.

Alo Accolade Crew Neck Pullover.

According to recent reports, alo is another longtime favorite at WH. The brand is known for its cozy, stylish (and premium-priced) loungewear. The fit is what we love most. The set, which comes in over a dozen colors, has an oversized feel, yet still manages to look intentional, says Deputy Features editor Carina Hsieh. “Unlike other sweatsuits, this one doesn’t look or feel unflattering or sloppy,” she says. She especially likes how it falls on her shoulders.

In a recent development, it’s also the “perfect transition-weather sweatsuit.” The French terry material is made up of 65% cotton and 35% polyester, for a “really soft, thick, and high-quality” feel. The fabric doesn’t feel ultra-heavy, though, so it’s a great pick for fall and spring when you might overheat in thicker sets. Another perk? The pants have pockets.

However, the sizing isn’t the most intuitive. Hsieh, who is typically a small or medium in other brands, is an extra-extra small in these pants. The pants also run a bit long. Hsieh notes sizing down is likely the way to go for this set.

Aritzia Cozy Sweatfleece Mega Funnel Neck.

Aritzia Cozy Sweatfleece Mega Jogger.

I had been hearing great things about Aritzia’s Sweatfleece line, and after testing for over a month, I can attest that it’s truly the coziest sweat set I’ve worn. Made from 78% cotton and 22% polyester, the material is soft with a fleece-lined interior. They’ll definitely keep you warm; that fleece inside is perfect for chilly temps. But they don’t feel too heavy. The material is still breathable, and I don’t get overheated when I’m wearing them.

In a recent development, I also love the look of this set, especially with the funnel/mockneck style—which is very on-trend. I have been wearing the suit when I work from home, and it makes me feel put together and chic, even though I’m in the coziest clothes I own. I’m also a runner, and I've noticed that this is the first thing I want to put on after I shower post-run. It’s the ultimate comfy outfit for recovery.

When it comes to sizing, these sweats have a “mega” fit, which means they’re oversized. I still sized up just to make sure mine would be roomy, but learned that I didn’t need to. These give you an oversized fit at your true size. Plus, as a shorter girlie (5’2!), I was thrilled that they came in short, regular, and long lengths. They’re still just the tiniest bit long, so I flip the elastic on each ankle under to shorten the legs. You can’t tell a thing!

Set Active Staple SET Uniform Layered Crewneck.

Set Active Staple Straight Leg Sweatpants.

This vintage-inspired sweatsuit from Set Active is made from 100% cotton, for those who want to prioritize more natural fibers. “I love how soft they feel,” Hsieh claims. “Sometimes 100% cotton feels stiff to me, and I’ve found that cotton sweats in particular lay weirdly at the chest when they’re oversized, but these maintain their plushy softness.”.

Recent findings suggest that this set is mid-weight, cozy, and warm. “I love a crewneck and sweatpants to sleep in, but sometimes find other sweats to be too much underneath my many layers of comforter and other blankets. These are the perfect weight to be warm and let me sleep comfortably,” Hsieh says. The crewneck isn't too bulky either—a challenge for a lot of sweatshirts—and fits easily underneath a jacket.

This set comes in tons of bold colorways, with contrasting collars and retro logos on the crewneck—so it’s great for anybody who's into the vintage activewear look. The only con? Hsieh, who is 5’3, found that pants run slightly long.

lululemon Scuba Oversized Full-Zip Hoodie.

lululemon Scuba Mid-Rise Wide-Leg Pant.

It has been revealed that this lululemon hoodie was named the best zip-up in our guide to the best hoodies for its comfy, classic fit. Where the hoodie shines, according to Associate Style & Commerce Editor Shannen Zitz, the pants are just as impressive. Both stand out for the waffle material: A soft, stretchy blend of cotton, modal, and polyester. She finds it more breathable than some of her buttery-smooth cotton sweats. Another perk? It’s basically immune to pilling.

It has been revealed that “Both pieces are incredibly soft and cozy,” Zitz claims. “I love the slightly oversized, waist-length fit of the top. It pairs really well with the matching sweatpants, which are equally comfy and have a flattering drape with a straight-leg fit.”.

This set styled with a plain white tee underneath and a pair of comfortable sneakers “happens to be my travel fit of choice,” she claims. “The hoodie keeps me warm and cozy during cold flights and early morning departure days, but I can easily unzip it or tie it around my waist if I get too warm.”.

Vuori Restore Straight Leg Sweatpant.

In a recent development, the Restore hoodie is one of Vuori’s best sellers, and for good reason. “I love the material,” Richey claims. “It’s very soft and feels super durable.” The French terry material (a cotton blend that’s smooth on the outside with brushed fleece on the inside)is made of breathable cotton and sturdy polyester.

As far as sweat sets go, this one has a lot of heft. The Restore line is thicker and denser than the label's BlissBlend or DreamKnit lines, making this set incredibly warm with a high-quality, structured feel. “The softness seems to also stay wash after wash, which is a huge win!” Richey adds.

Industry observers note that when it comes to fit, the hoodie has a perfectly oversized shape, but you might benefit from sizing up in the bottoms, particularly if you’re thicker-thighed, Ritchey claims. The pant comes in short, regular, and long lengths, giving you even more options to find the right fit.

Industry observers note that this Spanx set stands out as a lighter-weight and more polished option. “This set feels so light and airy,” notes Zitz. Spanx’s Air Essentials is made of their signature Spacer Fabric (a blend of modal, polyester, and elastane), for an ultra-smooth feel with plenty of stretch.

It has been revealed that “It’s one of the most comfortable lounge sets I own, but also one of the nicest looking,” Zitz states. The structured half-zip top and tailored (yet roomy) wide-leg pant have an almost dressed-up look, so you can wear the set to lounge or out of the house. It also comes in nearly 20 colors—a range of neutrals to bright options like red, blue, and plum.

Recent findings suggest that there is one downside: Neither the top nor bottom has pockets. While they might take away from the streamlined look, being able to slip your phone or wallet into a small pocket would be a bonus.

Gap VintageSoft Oversized Henley Pullover.

Gap VintageSoft Baggy Wide-Leg Sweatpants.

Gap certainly holds its own in the loungewear category. Aside from the cozy feel (thanks to a blend of cotton and polyester), it really shines when it comes to style.

“I love a wide-leg sweatpant,” Zitz notes. “I find they look less loungey than a jogger, and this pair is roomy without swallowing up my entire frame.” Even better is the henley top: The button-up design and mock neck make this top look more chic than your average crewneck or half-zip. “It’s unlike any other sweatshirt I own in terms of style,” Zitz says.

Sources indicate that one area for improvement: The color options. Our tester opted for a soft blue color, but would have preferred a more neutral gray—it just wasn’t in stock due to the limited colorways.

Rhone DreamGlow Barrel Leg Pant.

It has been revealed that rhone is another label that the WH fitness and style editors love. I have personally been a fan of their DreamGlow line for a while. It’s warm, but also has a sleek feel to it. There’s no heaviness to this set at all.

According to recent reports, made primarily of polyester and a small amount of elastane, the fabric also contains lyocell, a semi-synthetic fiber that helps to wick moisture away from the body, creating a slightly cooling effect. This set is ideal for anyone who runs hot or for transitional spring or fall weather. I like to wear it around my apartment on work-from-home days or as a travel outfit.

Sources indicate that this is also the set for someone who is a little sweatsuit-reluctant. The top has a slightly cropped and boxy fit, while the pants are a barrel-leg shape (a.k.a. a flared mid-leg and tapered ankle). Combined with the ultra-smooth material, this set looks less frumpy than your old-school sweat suits.

Hyundai reveals latest 7-seat Neira electric SUV

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (444 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hyundai revealed the production-ready Neira EV for the first time, a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV set to launch in Indonesia on November 20.
  • After introducing the Neira Concept at the 2026 Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show (GIIAS) in July, Hyundai is gearing up to open pre-orders on November 20.
  • The Neira is a pretty “big” deal as Hyundai’s first locally produced seven-seat electric SUV in Indonesia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai revealed the production-ready Neira EV for the first time, a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV set to launch in Indonesia on November 20.

After introducing the Neira Concept at the 2026 Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show (GIIAS) in July, Hyundai is gearing up to open pre-orders on November 20.

The Neira is a pretty “big” deal as Hyundai’s first locally produced seven-seat electric SUV in Indonesia.

Ahead of its official debut on Friday at GAIKINDO Auto Week (GAW) 2026, Hyundai offered a closer look at the upcoming Neira.

The electric SUV is essentially a Hyundai-badged version of the Kia Carens Clavis EV that debuted last year. Aside from the Hyundai logos, a few minor tweaks to the front and rear ends, and new wheels and headlights, it’s a near replica.

Inside, both are equipped with dual 12.3″ instrument display and center navigation screens, plus an added climate control panel.

Hyundai didn’t reveal battery or powertrain specs, but the Neira is expected to use the same 42 kWh and 51.4 kWh battery packs as the Carens Clavis EV. The former offers an MIDC range of up to 251 mi (404 km), while the latter has up to 304 mi (490 km) on a single charge.

Both batteries can be charged from 10% to 80% in around 39 minutes using a 100 kW DC fast charger.

The Kia Carens Clavis is 4,550 mm long, 1,800 mm wide, and 1,708 mm tall, with a 2,780 mm wheelbase, so Hyundai’s Neira will likely be about the same size, if not slightly bigger.

Hyundai noted the Neira has four key advantages: A higher ground clearance, Hyundai Bluelink connectivity tech, a Blind-spot View Monitor (BVM), and easy third-row access.

A post shared by Hyundai Motors Indonesia (@hyundaimotorindonesia).

Ahead of its upcoming launch, Hyundai is taking the electric 7-seater on a trip to prove its capabilities, going from Kilometer Nol in Banda Aceh to Banda Neira, which is about 4,000 kilometers (about 2,500 miles).

IT’s AN OFT-EXPRESSED sentiment, but it’s true: The holidays turn people’s attention toward friends, family, and community. There’s a beauty in the selfless, caring gifts people give to others. And while all that giving feels great, the holidays are also a good time to treat yourself. Plus, it’s getting colder.

Whether you equate The North Face with everyday city wear or outdoor adventures, it’s a solid, time-tested spot to get a gift for a loved one (or yourself). The brand has jackets and accessories with familiar winter looks, as well as products with less expected silhouettes that still offer protection from the elements in an understated style.

Here’s a look at some of the best cold-weather gear that will have you wrapping up the gift of warmth and durability… even if that gift is for yourself.

This is an easy gifting win because the warm, hooded, insulated jacket is a recognizable The North Face staple, evoking an unpretentious spin on the brand’s iconic Nuptse Jacket.

In a recent development, it’s familiar, but it’s also practical—the kind of gift you feel good about because it’s going to get a ton of use. (And it can withstand the repeated wears.) The attached hood offers protection from biting winds, and the straightforward color options make it easy to pair with a variety of outfits, whether it’s something fun or part of a heavy bundling during the coldest days of winter. This is the perfect type of winter coat: warm but not too puffy.

The Zaneck Jacket is a great alternative to the Aconcagua, stepping away from the outdoorsy look the brand is best known for. It’s still waterproof and insulated, but it has a longer, more modern cut.

The Zaneck comes with a removable faux fur lining for the hood, which, in addition to being warm, means there are a couple of different looks that can be teased out of it. The straight cuffs add to its stylish feel in a way that doesn’t scream “I’m dressed for warmth and not fashion,” even though it’s doing both.

Recent findings suggest that the Lone Peak Triclimate 2 has a lot in common with the Zaneck. From a distance, they cut a similar silhouette. However, the Lone Peak adds a little versatility if you’re looking for a jacket that can handle a variety of climates.

In a recent development, A removable, insulated inner jacket is attached to a removable, insulated top layer, which is fit for rainy conditions or as a spring or fall jacket. The insulated layer converts the whole thing into a winter-ready jacket. It also sports underarm vents capable of releasing heat in the middle of a long hike, ideal for outdoorsy types. The hood is removable and it’s got adjustable cuffs and an adjustable hem, making this a do-it-all jacket.

Sources indicate that it might be easy to ignore the Pertex Jacket. It’s a bit unassuming. It doesn’t cut as stylish of a figure as the Zaneck, but it’s endlessly useful. The lightweight Pertex fabric will keep you dry in a downpour, but it also offers warmth without marshmallow-like bulk.

The lightweight aspect makes this the kind of coat you toss in the backseat on the way to a hike, just in case. It’s also great for layering, whether it’s tossed on over a sweater or layered under an overcoat to make a favorite jacket more winter-ready.

Recent findings suggest that this edition of the classic Base Camp Duffel echoes the design details we love in The North Face’s jackets. While it’s got enough style and a heap of color options for daily use, it’s built for adventure.

According to recent reports, made with water- and tear-resistant fabric, it boasts 71 liters of storage space, a roomier option to the similar 31-liter version. Like all of the brand’s products, it’s built as if the designers have been through the rigors of outdoor adventures (and they probably have). It’s got a sweeping D-zip opening, backpack straps, mesh pockets, and compression straps in case you’re curious if you can pack 73 liters worth of gear into the 71-liter space. (You know you’ve tried.).

According to recent reports, the North Face has a lot of hats, none more iconic than this. The Salty Lined Beanie has a classic feel, fitting snuggly over the head with rib-knit texture, a cuffed shape, soft fabric, and ample color options to ensure it will match any jacket or accessory. The Salty Lined Beanie encapsulates the entire The North Face vibe in a small way: It’s stylish enough for a subway ride to work and practical enough for an outdoor adventure. Best of all, it’ll keep your ears warm in either instance.

In a recent development, often, the best glove is the one that disappears into the outfit. It looks seamless, keeping hands warm without drawing too much attention. The Etip Recycled Glove is about functionality first and foremost, but the simple design and understated colors makes it look good with a variety of winter outfits.

Recent findings suggest that while we all like to pretend we aren’t attached to our phones, the Etip makes a great modern gift because its stretchy fleece delivers a snug fit and the palms have touchscreen compatibility. That means you won’t have to take off your gloves to respond to that vital text while the snow is falling.

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Iceland’s first wind farm comes with a water-saving bonus

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1297 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.
  • It has been revealed that vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads.
  • Landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power manufacturer, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.

It has been revealed that vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads. And Iceland’s windiest months coincide with the time of year when less water flows into its reservoirs.

Landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power manufacturer, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026. The first 14 turbines are online; another 14 will be installed in a second phase, and the entire wind farm is expected to be operating by the end of 2027.

Once complete, Vaðölduver will have 120 megawatts (MW) of capacity. When I met with the folks at Landsvirkjun in Reykjavik last month, they told me that’s enough to power the equivalent of 90,000 Icelandic households. Vaðalda’s electricity feeds into the grid and is sold through power purchase agreements.

Vaðölduver sits on a lava-and-sand plain east of the Þjórsá River, south of Sultartangi Dam. Landsvirkjun already operates seven hydropower stations in the surrounding Þjórsá and Tungnaá region.

The wind farm was sited in this region of Iceland because the seasons line up nicely.

The winds are strongest in winter, when inflows into hydropower reservoirs can be low. In summer, wind speeds tend to drop, but glacial melt increases water availability for the hydropower system.

When the wind turbines are generating plenty of electricity, Landsvirkjun can ease off hydropower and leave more water in its reservoirs. When the wind drops, hydropower can pick up more of the demand.

That gives the utility more control over when it uses its stored water and helps that water go further.

German wind turbine maker Enercon manufactured Vaðölduver’s turbines. The project also includes a service and maintenance agreement with Enercon.

Sources indicate that landsvirkjun had a decade of experience operating pilot wind turbines before building Vaðölduver. One big thing they learned: They didn’t need tall towers to find plenty of wind.

Industry observers note that there’s little vegetation or other surface obstructions across this unique, exposed landscape. That allows the turbines to capture productive winds closer to the ground than they could at a more wooded or sheltered location.

“Lower” is relative, of course. The turbines still reach 150 meters (492 feet) at their highest blade tip.

Recent findings suggest that the wind farm covers 17.1 square kilometers (6.6 square miles). Twenty-five turbines are rated at 4.26 MW each, and the remaining three at 4.5 MW. Landsvirkjun’s presentation puts annual generation at 440 GWh and lists a P50 net efficiency figure of 43%, which is considered strong for onshore wind.

The ability to tap into existing infrastructure was a major factor in Landsvirkjun’s site selection. Where a wind farm goes affects its cost, its environmental footprint, and the people who live nearby.

It has been revealed that landsvirkjun also identifies active engagement with communities and other stakeholders as essential to building wind projects. At Vaðölduver, the immediate task is to finish the remaining 14 turbines while the first phase completes its trial runs.

The company sees wind as a potential third pillar of Iceland’s electricity supply alongside hydropower and geothermal. Vaðölduver demonstrates how those resources can work together, with wind adding generation while helping conserve stored water.

Iceland is a world leader in clean energy. It generates nearly 100% of its electricity from renewable sources, combining hydropower fueled by glacial runoff and rivers (around 70%) and geothermal energy (around 30%).

Over 90% of Icelandic households use direct geothermal hot water for space heating and hot water, while the remaining homes use renewable electricity.

But it’s got the same grid capacity challenges as every other country. Adding wind – and anything else that uses power – means paying close attention to what the grid can handle. Iceland has an isolated transmission system, so maintaining stability and ensuring sufficient capacity are increasingly important as the country develops more projects.

It has been revealed that while in Reykjavik, I met with the Minister of the Environment, Energy and Climate, Jóhann Páll Jóhannsson, who told me that the Icelandic grid’s capacity is expected to grow from 20 TWh to 24-25 TWh within a decade. Jóhannsson also remarked that he is pro-data center and that investors are keen to establish more of them in the country.

It has been revealed that when I asked Jóhannsson and his team, as well as the teams at Landsvirkjun and publicly owned ON Power, Iceland’s second-largest electricity generator and largest EV charger network, about grid expansion prepares to handle that pipeline, they all remarked that legislative reforms were being passed to speed up energy permitting processes. There is also financing in place to grow the grid. The physical transmission network is being expanded, but the process is slow because NIMBYism is creating bottlenecks.

In learning about newly introduced and completed Icelandic power projects during my visit, it was apparent that the companies in the power and geothermal heat sector regularly collaborate on projects – everyone brings their expertise to the table and works for the common good (yes, really).

Sources indicate that but what was striking in discussions about grid expansion was that there seemed to be no plans to pitch in with the Icelandic transmission system operator (TSO), Landsnet hf. It seemed that the initiative was to let the TSO come up with the solutions on its own. At most, Jóhannsson’s team said its legislative reform “opened the door” to possible grid innovations.

When I asked the Landsvirkjun team whether they were considering working with the TSO on distributed energy resource (DER) projects like virtual power plants and onsite battery storage for its heavy-industry clients, which make up 80% of its business, they remarked they hadn’t considered it.

According to recent reports, I often wonder why Quebec hasn't followed this strategy. They have huge dams with world-leading power connections, and one of the issue they are facing is a lack of water to refill those dams, due to several years of relative drought. I know it costs a lot to build wind power up north, but siting a project there would re-use their massive investment in power lines. The dams would act as gigantic batteries, because they wouldn't need to drain their reservoirs when the wind is blowing.

Iceland has earned its reputation as a clean energy leader. Bringing that same collaborative and creative approach to expanding its grid would help it keep setting an example for the rest of the world.

  • Recent findings suggest that the secret lies in layered lighting, which involves a series of soft illumination sources working together in concert: A bedside lamp provides focused task lighting for reading, while wall sconces free up valuable nightstand space and introduce a soft diffused glow.
  • Industry observers note that dimmable fixtures and warm white light bulbs can be especially transformational in bedrooms that also function as an office or a hangout space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when you’re trying to unwind at the end of a long day, turning on the “massive light” is simply not the move. The glare of a way-too-bright overhead light is not only unflattering but oftentimes overstimulating. It can make your otherwise cozy bedroom feel more like a department-store dressing room, leaving relaxation a little bit harder to come by. The right bedroom lighting, on the other hand, can bring a sense of warmth, atmosphere, and visual interest to the space where you spend some of your most cherished downtime.

Recent findings suggest that the secret lies in layered lighting, which involves a series of soft illumination sources working together in concert: A bedside lamp provides focused task lighting for reading, while wall sconces free up valuable nightstand space and introduce a soft diffused glow. Floor lamps can brighten an otherwise neglected corner, and a beautiful chandelier or pendant light doubles as a bedroom’s focal point, even when the light is switched off.

Industry observers note that dimmable fixtures and warm white light bulbs can be especially transformational in bedrooms that also function as an office or a hangout space. Ahead, we’ve rounded up our favorite bedroom lighting ideas, including sculptural statement pieces, portable table lamps, and wall-mounted fixtures that usher in a sense of calm.

Recent findings suggest that for a reading nook, a work-from-home space, or just a little warm white lighting, a floor lamp can show off your taste without sacrificing functionality. We’ve pulled two designer-favorite must-haves for those in the world of interior design.

This 1960s model from Danish designer Mads Caprani hasn’t gone out of style since its release. The pleated shade, bentwood spine, and U-shaped cast-iron base make it one of the most easily recognized and iconic designs in floor lamps to this day. If you’re looking to make a statement about your style, this piece does just that—landing somewhere between studious and stylish, as in polo champion Nacho Figueras’s Florida home.

In a recent development, another lamp for tastemakers, this design from Isamu Noguchi has made the rounds in many celebrity home tours from a minimalist Brooklyn brownstone to Troye Sivan’s modern Melbourne home. Commerce director Rachel Fletcher has previously named a Noguchi lamp one of her bedroom essentials. The reputation of Noguchi’s work and the unique style of his Akari lamps make this a design staple for anyone hoping to cultivate a modern bedroom.

According to recent reports, we love the look of dual table lamps to frame your bed and create a distinct visual space in your bedroom. It also allows your bed to feel like a conscious design choice instead of a strictly functional piece. We’re taking bedside lamp notes from this Portland home owned by the lead singer of The Shins and decorated by Jessica Helgerson. And, if you don’t want to do things matchy-matchy, any one of these lamps would look great solo too.

We love this moody metallic option from Article for a midcentury look—and we named it one of our favorite bedside lamps after ample editor testing. At $149, the price is also right.

According to recent reports, if you’re struggling to find a table lamp that plays well with others, this is a viable option from coastal core experts Serena & Lily. This comes in four beautiful shades, inspired by the Italian shoreline, and there’s even a touch of rattan for a beachy bedside table moment.

The Flos Bellhop table lamp is a great source of ambient light in this minimalist Barcelona bedroom.

A godsend for a bedroom with inconvenient outlets, these design-forward portable lamps bring both ambience and task lighting wherever you need them.

It has been revealed that another favorite of interior designers, the Flos Bellhop table lamp is a great source of ambient light in a minimalist setting. These super-portable LED lamps have four dimmer settings, are USB-compatible, and can last up to 24 hours on a single charge. And, if you love the simple glass shape, they’re also available as wall sconces for a stylish outdoor lighting moment.

In a recent development, you never know when you’ll need a little extra light, and the Poldina Pro can adapt to your ever-changing needs. The lamp pairs a petite silhouette with the clean lines of Italian minimalist design, making it a versatile fit for your nightstand, dresser, or reading nook. Without any unsightly wires to speak of, the lamp can appear as an intentional design choice just about anywhere. Its touch-sensitive dimmer lets you adjust the brightness and choose between three color temperatures.

AD shopping writer Julia Harrison, who tested the Micro version, appreciates its versatility for desk work and kitchen prep alike. She notes that the lamp “blends shyly and seamlessly into all setups that require a little, but not too much, light.” With approximately 12 hours of battery life, it’s an especially convenient option for adding a little extra illumination wherever you need it.

Wall lighting brings a warm dimension to the design of your bedroom and provides great task lighting for a bedtime read. While we love table lamps on matching nightstands, wall sconces bring an added degree of intentionality in their design, as seen in Walton Goggins’s guest bedroom and Jennifer Garner’s kid’s bedroom.

Sources indicate that available in 24 colors and with flexible orientation, this wall sconce channels the fun throwback design sensibility of Portland-based Schoolhouse. Not relegated to the bedroom alone, these fixtures can bring vibrancy to any space—as is evident in the bathroom of this timeless, edgy Massachusetts home.

Recent findings suggest that A visible mending detail modernizes a traditional style, so the pleated lampshade remains classic without being too precious. We love to imagine this lining a long entryway, or on either side of a tall headboard—the perfect lighting for bedtime pages.

Linen shades are classic for a reason: They soften the appearance of a light fixture, giving even the most straightforward silhouettes a dash of warmth and character. Quince’s Contemporary Sconce pairs crisp white linen shades with a streamlined steel frame, available in brass or black for two distinctly different looks. The brass finish befits a more traditional bedroom, while the black feels especially sharp juxtaposed against pale walls and minimalist decor. Choose a single or double configuration depending on your space, or install a matching pair on either side of the bed for a polished alternative to bedside table lamps.

Industry observers note that if a flower could moonlight as a light fixture, it would probably look something like Soho Home’s Florie Wall Light. A fluted, bubbled texture gives the glass an almost vintage quality, while the frosted finish diffuses the light into a soft, atmospheric glow. Even at just nine inches tall and nine inches wide, the fixture has enough personality to stand on its own, though opting for a pair to flank the bed would be an especially charming choice to imbue the space with a dash of romance.

Actress Laura Harrier hangs a bespoke pendant lamp in her bedroom.

According to recent reports, the wrong kind of flush mount can be an eyesore, and the right kind of pendant light can transform a space from tragic to tasteful. These picks from IKEA and Lumens are both contemporary yet classic, proving them a satisfying finishing touch that makes all the difference.

In a recent development, IKEA brings an affordable yet still-elevated style to the lineup with this ubiquitous, rattan-like pendant (technically latticed bamboo) from Ilse Crawford. We love this style as much for dining room lighting as we do for bedroom lighting. Can’t decide which? Two will only cost you $140 total.

According to recent reports, danish lighting design has a knack for making even the most practical objects feel like works of art. Case in point: the PH 5 Hanging Lamp. Its distinctive arrangement of overlapping shades creates a sculptural silhouette, with each layer directing and diffusing light. The three-shade system sends most of the illumination downward while allowing a softer glow to escape around the sides for ambient lighting. The result is a striking pendant that commands attention, even when it’s not turned on. The light would look especially beautiful suspended above a bedside table in place of a traditional lamp.

Supermodel Elsa Hosk incorporated a pink Tronchi chandelier, made of Murano glass, into her Upcoming York City bedroom.

Industry observers note that might some consider a chandelier too much for a bedroom? Yes, someone who needs to live a little. A chandelier brings a sense of occasion to every space it’s in, and your bedroom deserves no less. These picks bring elegance without overkill.

We love how supermodel Elsa Hosk incorporated a pink Tronchi chandelier made of Murano glass into her Upcoming York City bedroom, and you can find a similar pick on 1stDibs if you want to sleep in rose-colored bliss.

Often referred to as the “boob light,” this type of flush mount can get a bad rap, but West Elm has figured out how to make them shine. This contemporary ceiling light fixture is simple, aesthetic, and subtle.

According to recent reports, serena & Lily’s Capiz Scalloped Chandelier has the delicate charm of a seaside find, with a little extra glamour courtesy of its antique-gold framing. Each translucent capiz shell is individually hand-set, creating a softly scalloped silhouette that feels like a piece of jewelry for the ceiling. The natural variations in the shells’ shapes and opacity give the fixture a beautiful sense of movement. Light filters through the overlapping layers to cast a warm diffused glow, making it an especially lovely choice for a bedroom where atmosphere matters just as much as illumination.

If you’re looking for guidance when it comes to your bedroom lights, it’s important to keep a variety of factors in mind. Do you do a lot of reading in bed? Maybe table lamps should be your primary focus. Do you have enough fixtures to keep the space illuminated but not too bright? Perhaps a floor lamp or two will provide that glow for you. Are you spending most of your time winding down and heading to sleep? Try a night-light or string lights for ambience! And, of course, you’ll want multiple light sources to get the look (and the vibe) just right. Sources indicate that it’s become one of her favorite racerback sports bras and she’s consistently impressed by how well it holds her in during strength training classes. The cute, strappy back design definitely doesn’t hurt, either.

Recent findings suggest that another bonus: the fabric dries super promptly, so even when you break a sweat, you don’t have to worry about visible marks. Wohlner says she probably should’ve sized down for a more snug fit. That said, her usual medium still works, it just doesn’t have that extra-tight, compressive feel some of her high-impact bras do. We also wish it had adjustable straps for customizability.

Old solar panels have silver and copper worth recovering. A new US recycling company called Jupiter plans to send metals recovered from retired solar panels and data center hardware to Korea Zinc’s refineries, including a $7.4 billion plant planned for Clarksville, Tennessee.

Industry observers note that jupiter joins US solar panel recycler Solarcycle and PedalPoint Recycling, Korea Zinc’s US recycling and metals business, into a single, fully integrated firm. Jupiter says it’s launching with eight certified US facilities, nearly 1 million square feet of processing space, and about 250 employees. It’s also taking on customers from both businesses, including Microsoft, Prologis, and Brookfield.

It has been revealed that for a solar farm or data center operator, that means a single firm can take equipment out of service, resell parts with remaining useful life, and recycle the rest. Customers can track where the materials go and bring them back into their own supply chains.

In a recent development, korea Zinc will hold a majority stake. Solarcycle’s Suvi Sharma will lead Jupiter as CEO, and PedalPoint’s Kevin Hahm will be CFO. Microsoft and Prologis Ventures are among Solarcycle’s existing investors.

Industry observers note that as Electrek reported in January, Solarcycle’s Cedartown, Georgia, plant was processing thousands of old solar panels a week when it opened. Solarcycle said the plant could handle up to 5 gigawatts’ worth of panels annually at full capacity, recovering materials such as glass, aluminum, copper, and silver.

In a recent development, the Tennessee plant adds a US refining step. Korea Zinc is developing the facility, called Project Crucible, with US government backing. It expects to start production in phases in 2029. The plant is designed to process about 1.1 million tons of raw materials per year and produce roughly 540,000 tons of finished products.

Electric power tool brand Greenworks is expanding its battery-forward lineup in a huge way with the launch of OPTIMUS, an all-newly introduced, go-anywhere electric side-by-side utility vehicle that packs over 100 equivalent hp and a 40 mph top speed.

First shown at Equip Exposition 2026 in Kentucky last month, the newly redesigned Greenworks OPTIMUS UTV is the biggest, baddest, and newest addition to the company’s battery-backed commercial ecosystem. Greenworks claims the new SxS brings together the brand’s purpose-built equipment and power platforms and is designed to work across the demands of its professional property maintenance customers.

“OPTIMUS has always been about pushing battery power beyond what the industry expects, and the UTV is a natural extension of that vision,” says Yin Chen, CEO of Greenworks. “We’re bringing professionals more ways to put battery power to work, from the equipment they use to maintain properties to the utility vehicles and charging systems that support their entire operation.”.

Industry observers note that greenworks’ OPTIMUS is built around the organization’s 400V high-voltage electrical platform and mates a pair of compact electric motors that combine for 110 equivalent (?) hp. Those motors draw power from a 19 kWh lithium-ion battery pack with enough efficiency to hit a 40 MPH top speed and cover up to 68 miles of range under typical operating conditions.

When it’s time to haul, OPTIMUS offers buyers a 2,500 lb. towing capacity and 1,300 lb. payload capacity along with 11 full inches of ground clearance and a beefy, 6,000 lb. electric winch. Independent suspension, oversized all-terrain tires, torque vectoring differentials, and multiple terrain modes round out the spec sheet and a picture of a machine that’s designed to handle some seriously demanding off-road applications.

Looks expensive but for a gov or tech giant leasing or buying a latest utv probably price completive with less headache.

  • In a recent development, so, what is body recomp?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Body recomposition is the fitness goal these days. If you’ve been hearing the term everywhere like I have, and thinking body recompo-what, you’re not alone.

In a recent development, so, what is body recomp? Whether you knew it or not, chances are, you’ve probably pursued it at some point. If you’ve ever set out to reduce body fat or build muscle, you’ve been working toward a body recomposition goal. When people say body recomp these days, they really mean simultaneously losing fat and building muscle, not just one or the other.

Meet the expert: Brittany Busse, MD, is the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health.

Recent findings suggest that unlike simply losing weight, this approach isn’t about the number on the scale; it’s about improving the ratio of fat to muscle in your body for better health, performance, and aesthetics. (Oftentimes, when people talk about wanting to look "toned," they're really talking about body recomp, since you need low amounts of body fat to see the muscle you've built up.).

In a recent development, and, while body recomposition is completely possible, it can be a little more technical than other fitness goals. Here are the core things you need to know to get started on your body recomp journey.

Get started with our exclusive body recomp guide.

Recent findings suggest that first: a quick refresher. Body composition refers to a percentage breakdown of how much body fat, lean mass (that is, muscle!), and bone you've got on your body. Body recomposition is the process through which you change that breakdown.

These are the five most key things to keep in mind when trying to make that happen.

In a recent development, at the most basic level, losing fat requires a calorie deficit; you need to burn more than you consume. Working with a nutritionist or doctor, you can determine exactly what this means for you, but for body recomposition, it's only a slight deficit that you should be shooting for. We’re talking 250 to 500 calories max.

Keep in mind: “Weight loss should not be confused with fat loss,” Brittany Busse, MD, the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health previously told Women's Health. “Much of weight loss can also be loss of muscle mass.”.

According to recent reports, and, you don't want to lose muscle mass, particularly if your goal is body recomp. That’s why protein is critical, Dr. Busse says—but it’s just one piece of the puzzle. Tracking all three macros (protein, carbs, and fat) can go a long way in helping you stay full, energized, and strong while pursuing body recomp.

GET MORE INFO ABOUT COUNTING MACROS FOR BODY RECOMP WITH THE WH+ PDF.

Lifting is nonnegotiable. “People should weight train at least three times a week,” Dr. Busse said. “Weight training will build muscle mass, which will inevitably lead to improved metabolic health and fat loss.”.

In a recent development, keep up your cardio, too. But, if you’re a HIIT addict, you may want to try slowing things down. “Zone 2 cardio is the most effective way to burn fat while sparing muscle. This is exercising at a level where you can hold a ‘breathy’ conversation comfortably for 45-60 minutes,” Dr. Busse said. “Walking on an incline, cycling, and rucking are all examples of Zone 2 workouts,” she said.

It's hard to come up with a training proposal all on your own, so relying on the expertise of trainers to create a program can help make sure you're working your muscles efficiently and effectively.

Women's Health+ has many body recomp-focused programs for people of all experience levels: the 4-Week Walking Initiative, the 4-Week Strength Training Plan, the 4-Week Build & Burn Series (which allows you to follow along with dumbbell, barbell, or kettlebell-based workouts), and the Body Recomp Guide.

Age, hormones, and genetics all play a role in body composition, as does access to high-quality food and medical care. Not everyone has the same amount of time to spend exercising. So, take it easy on yourself, and if you can, get help and support as you work toward your goals.
